result.title: Satisficing as competitive Bayesian weighting: a minimal model of goal-directed choice under an unattained target
result.summary: Animals and humans often do not maximize; they act relative to goals (aspiration levels) that are frequently not yet met. How can a goal that is not (yet) realized organize choice? Deacon (2012) calls such absence-referenced organization \emph{ententional}, and García-Valdecasas and Deacon (2024) argue that ends are best understood as constraints rather than as particular states. We examine this idea in a minimal formal setting: Risk-sensitive Satisficing (RS), a bandit learning rule that values each action by its share of past trials multiplied by its surplus or shortfall relative to an aspiration level. We show that RS can be rewritten as a Bayesian-like estimator, Attention Competitive Bayes (ACB), in which the aspiration level is the prior mean of every action and the finite budget of trials sets how strongly evidence can override it. Two consequences follow. First, actions that are no longer sampled are partially overridden by the goal rather than by past observations: their estimates relax toward the aspiration level without any data being discarded. This ``pseudo-forgetting'' distinguishes ACB from models with an explicit forgetting rate. Second, when the aspiration is unattainable, exploration does not settle; in Bernoulli bandit simulations, adjusting the aspiration level from evidence reduced regret (expected loss). ACB offers an analyzable model in which an unattained goal and a limited attentional resource jointly constrain behavior, and it yields testable predictions about how organisms revalue options they have abandoned.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把风险敏感满意化（RS）赌博机规则改写为类贝叶斯估计器 ACB：以抱负水平作为各动作先验均值、以有限试次预算决定证据覆盖强度，并分析其「伪遗忘」与目标不可达时探索不收敛的现象。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「未达成目标作为先验约束、有限注意力预算限制证据、目标不可达则探索不止」的表述，可能为 LVR 中停止决策与计算预算分配提供概念类比，是否可用于解释「继续思考 vs 停止」的动态尚待核查。
